Subject: Billing split & VAT/GST validation for Q2 invoice

Hi Mateo,

We’re getting ready to process Redwood’s Q2 invoice, but tax wants the charge split between our EU purchasing entity and our APAC entity for accounting reasons. Can you confirm Redwood can: 

- Issue either (a) a single invoice with line-level entity allocation and tax codes, or (b) two invoices (EU / APAC) tied to the same contract.
- Validate the EU VAT ID below via VIES and confirm reverse-charge applicability.
- Confirm whether Redwood needs a self-billing arrangement or if HydroCore should route a PO to accounts@redwood.com.

Entities & IDs:
- HydroCore Europe B.V. (Netherlands) — VAT NL123456789B01
- HydroCore Asia Pte Ltd (Singapore) — UEN 202301234X (GST)

We attached our tax certificates and a brief note from our AP team about GST withholding expectations in SG. The split would be 70% to HydroCore Europe B.V. and 30% to HydroCore Asia. Please let us know what documentation you need from our side and a rough timeline so we can align treasury.

Thanks,
Emma Jones

Hi Emma — thanks for the clear breakdown and the attachments. We can support both approaches (single invoice with line-level tax allocation, or two invoices) but there are bookkeeping and tax implications either way. Quick notes: 

- We will validate the EU VAT ID via VIES and confirm reverse-charge applicability for the NL entity.
- Singapore UENs are outside VIES — for GST treatment we need either a GST registration certificate or evidence of Singapore tax residency for the purchasing entity.
- For self-billing: Redwood can accommodate a self-billing flow, but Finance needs an explicit PO or a signed self-billing agreement from HydroCore.

Internal next steps (looping in Marissa & Ben): Marissa — can you run the VIES check and capture a screenshot? Ben — legal/ops: please advise on self-billing vs our usual PO workflow and whether we can create a single invoice with per-line entity allocations in our accounting system (QuickBooks/NetSuite mapping).

If HydroCore confirms you want two invoices, we’ll produce them and target sending them by EOD Tue (2026-06-22). If you prefer a single invoice with split lines, we’ll draft a sample invoice and send it for sign-off.

I’ll wait for confirmation of which route you prefer and any additional docs you can attach for the Singapore UEN.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales

Hi team — done and recommendations below. Attachments: vies_check_nl123456789B01.png.

1) VIES: NL123456789B01 is valid (screenshot attached). Reverse-charge applies for B2B SaaS where the customer is established in the EU and provides a valid VAT ID. We should mark those line items as "reverse-charge (RC) — VAT 0%" on the EU invoice and include the reference: "VAT to be accounted for by the customer under Article 196 VAT Directive".

2) Singapore UEN: the screenshot Emma provided shows GST enrollment but not a GST certificate. For tax purposes in SG we recommend HydroCore either provide their GST registration document or we route the 30% charge to HydroCore Asia Pte Ltd and note GST as 0% if reverse-charge applies (depending on whether local withholding applies). I’ll coordinate with tax counsel if we need an explicit certificate of entitlement.

3) Invoicing approach: two invoices is cleaner for customer accounting. For internal mapping: create two invoice numbers (INV-RED-9821-EU and INV-RED-9821-APAC), link both to the same Deal ID in HubSpot / NetSuite, and map revenue recognition to the contract. Ben — confirm accounting fields for APAC tax code mapping (I propose tax code RC for EU, GST-EX for APAC until we receive official docs).

Next steps: Mateo to send draft invoices; I’ll attach the VIES screenshot to the HubSpot record and archive the HydroCore certificates in the secure drive.

Marissa Cole
